This relay *is* that engine for the purposes of the DM enumeration: it reads the ops `:messaging` enqueued through `Outbox.enqueue` and writes back the delivery rows and outcome the engine would have written (the recipe `DmOutcomeTest` pinned in S7), on the **raw** connection, so Phase 7's statements do not enter `:messaging`'s event stream and "crash at k" keeps meaning something about `:messaging`. Its three phases are §15.3's relay events, including "timeout after apply". **What this costs, named:** the scenario texts of §15.3 say "3 relays over 2 operators, one refusing" (SCN-A) and similar relay-set shapes, and *which of three relays* refused is not expressible here — only *what outcome* a store got, through `ModelDmRelay.outcomeFor`. Every node still carries four relay slots over two operators so the namespace, capability and registration rows have the shape the invariants read. **Hostile modes: five, and every one of them is exercised by a case.** SHUFFLE and REPEATS (SCN-B and the seeded worlds), WITHHOLD (the seeded worlds), TRUNCATE (the RP9 case), and **LIE_FAILED** — new here, which stores the blob and tells the sender it failed, and is the only way to reach D3 from the outside, since every other duplicate a sender can produce carries identical bytes and dies at D1 (see item 5). §15.1's other modes are **not** implemented, and the list is deliberately not longer than the cases: REWIND, RESURRECT, STALL, SHORT_EXPIRY, LONG_EXPIRY, DELAY_RELEASE, COPY_NAMESPACE, WITHHOLD_NEWEST_BUNDLE, LOSE_KEYS, ATTACKER_REGISTERS, REFUSE_ONE_SENDER, WITHHOLD_ALL_BUNDLES. RESURRECT, DELAY_RELEASE and REFUSE_ONE_SENDER were written and then removed: all three worked, none had a case, and a hostile mode nothing drives is a claim about the harness rather than a property of the engine. COPY_NAMESPACE was written, driven, and removed for a better reason — see item 7 on RP3 |
| 5 | §15.3 table, §15.5, §15.7 | **What is implemented, and what each piece of it kills.** Seven of §15.3's twelve scenarios — **SCN-A** (send), **SCN-B** (receive and reorder under SHUFFLE and REPEATS), **SCN-D** (key change, with the forged-binding case), **SCN-F** (ephemeral, with the clock stepped back), **SCN-G** (outcomes and the identical-bytes resend), **SCN-J** (faults, both halves) and **SCN-L** (migration safety plus traffic on the migrated file) — with the double crashes §15.3 names for SCN-A, SCN-B and SCN-F, the "timeout after apply" run at every relay event, and `SQLITE_FULL` enumerated over every write and every commit of SCN-J. Four functional-suite sub-cases. Three of them are each the *only* case that can kill a mutant this slice registers: **RP6** (re-encryption after a wrongly reported FAILED — the one path that reaches D3, because every other duplicate a sender can make carries identical bytes and dies at D1), the **§12.3 rejected-request replay** (the one that reaches D2b), and an **EP** read-path expiry case (the behavioural half of the DAO lint). **The defects this slice found in the engine, and the one it found and left alone.**

**Found and fixed: `Messaging.send` and `Messaging.retry` could *throw* `STORAGE_FULL` instead of
answering it.** `SendStep.send` catches `StorageFullException` around the enqueue transaction and
maps it to `Outcome.STORAGE_FULL`, which the facade turns into `SendResult.STORAGE_FULL` — but the
**planning** transaction that runs before it was outside the catch, and it writes (the minute index,
and with `createOffer` the offered root), so its commit is a place a full disk lands. On a device
with a full disk the facade call would have thrown. `retry` had the same shape. Both now catch, and
nothing has committed at that point, so there is nothing to undo. Two things about *how* it was
found are worth recording. It is invisible to a sampled enumeration and appeared only at
`-Dghost.dm.crash=full`, which is the argument for the gate scale existing at all. And it is
invisible to an injector that fires `SQLITE_FULL` at a `SELECT`: the first version of the harness
did, the first failure it produced was a read, and "the engine does not map a failure SQLite cannot
produce" is not a finding — narrowing the injection to writes and commits is what made the *real*
one legible.

**Found in review and fixed: the same shape survived in two more places, and the first of them is
another facade call that throws.** `SendStep.sendControl`'s planning transaction was outside a
catch, exactly as `send`'s had been, and `sendControl` is what `Messaging.resetSession(contact):
SendResult` calls — so on a full disk `resetSession` threw where `SendResult.STORAGE_FULL` exists
to be returned. Nothing found it because **no scenario drives `resetSession`**: SCN-J's script is
send, receive and sweep. It is also the path the scheduled reconnect and revocation controls take,
where a throw is worse than it looks, because the scheduled row is retired in the send's own
transaction and a throw before that keeps re-planning the same notice. The second is `flushOne`,
whose planning transaction was outside its own `catch (StorageFullException)`: one item's transient
ended the **whole** flush pass, deferring every other contact's pending item. §21.7 point 4 names a
full disk as a transient retried at the next pass, for one item, and that is what it does now.

**Found and left alone: `DmActor` swallows whatever a pass throws, and that is correct.**
`runPass` rethrows, and `wake` submits the pass to a single-thread executor whose future nobody
reads — so on a device an exception out of a pass ends that pass and nothing else, and the work is
owed again at the next trigger. A harness that called `runPass` directly and let the exception out
would be testing a device that does not exist; one that swallowed it silently would hide every bug
a pass has. `DmCrashWorld` therefore records them and the runner asserts what may be in the list:
**nothing at all** in a fault-free run, and **only `SQLITE_FULL`** in a run that injected one. That
assertion is what turned the first `SQLITE_FULL` enumeration red, and it is worth keeping for
exactly that reason.

### 22.16 Forward notes (S11 implementation, 2026-09-22)

**Precedence.** These notes record what slice S11 (the privacy worlds: T32, the T34 seizure world,
T35, the recorded S-DM2/S-DM4 baselines, the 40 privacy mutants, `dm-privacy-gate.yml`, and the T2
changes of §4.9) delivered where the sections above say something else, and what it deliberately
did not deliver. They win over §0–§21 and over §22.0–§22.15 for the items they name, and for nothing
else.

S11 is, like S10, far larger than one slice, and this slice closes a **vertical** part of it rather
than touching every part: the world, eight of the ten exact joins, two of the seven twins, one of
the four statistics, the seizure world with its one-reply variant but without its Olm half, T35 as
far as the tags reach, ten of the forty mutants, the gate that runs them, and §4.9's client model and
report (not its gate-scale baselines). Items 1–9 and 16 are what was built; items 10–15 and 20 are the
deferrals and deviations, by name; items 17–19 and 21 are what the slice and its review found.
**Nothing in the report claims a check the run did not make:** `dm-report-check.sh` pins the lines
this slice writes — eight joins, NI-DM1, NI-DM3, S-DM3, T34 and its one-reply variant, T35 and
`dm privacy mutants: 10 run, 10 detected` — and refuses the design's larger numbers until the tests
behind them exist.

| 1 | §15.6 "World", §15.1 "Clients" | **The privacy world** (`android/messaging/src/test/.../dmworld/`, `PrivacyWorld`). ### 22.17 Forward notes (S12 implementation, 2026-09-22)

**Precedence.** These notes record what slice S12 (app wiring and emulator: `MessagingWiring`, R8
rules, the manifest receiver, T12 with the grown native library, `dm-emulator.yml` with the
host/Android equivalence test, the `gate` build type, `scripts/device/dm-gate.sh`, the digest
export, the host re-store tool, and the S1 relays on staging; §17.1, §21.13) delivered where the
sections above say something else, and what it did not deliver. They win over §0–§21 and over
§22.0–§22.15 for the items they name, and for nothing else. (§22.16 is S11's.)

**The one thing to read first.** Everything in this slice that needs an Android device or an
emulator has been **built and not run**: no emulator or system image exists on the machine the slice
was written on, no device was attached, and the self-hosted runners' KVM (A17) is unverified. Every
APK the emulator job installs was assembled locally and inspected (item 11), and the run script and
the report check were driven end to end against a fake emulator; the suites themselves have never
executed on Android, and no run of `dm-emulator.yml` on any runner has been observed. Exit-gate item
10 of §17.2 ("emulator job green on API 29 and API 35") is therefore **open**, and nothing here
claims otherwise. The same holds for the device orchestrator and the gate instrumentation: tested
against fakes on a host, never on a phone. Item 17 records what the slice's review found.

**Precedence.** These notes record what slice S13 (PQ-C: `seal_root_pq`, `pq_key`, the slack rule,
the cadence, `pq_announced_week`, `offer_env`, the PQ3 healing world and the ProVerif model; §9.4,
§9.5, §17.1) delivered where the sections above say something else, and what it did not deliver.
They win over §0–§21 and over §22.0–§22.17 for the items they name, and for nothing else.

**The one thing to read first.** *(Superseded on 2026-09-24 by §22.31: the models were run, the
hash is pinned, and every query matched.)* The ProVerif models of item 12 **have never been run**: ProVerif is
not installed on the machine the slice was written on, nothing was downloaded to get it, and the
`pq-model` job fails closed until the owner commits the release's SHA-256 (item 12). The models were
checked by reading them against §6.4, §6.3, §9.4 and §9.5, and the comparison script by fourteen
fixtures run through a fake ProVerif; **no query result exists**, a syntax error in a `.pv` file
would first show on the runner, and the row's exit condition "M-1 … M-7 green in `pq-model`" is
**open** — and would stay open after a green run, which covers less than M-1 … M-7 (item 17).
Everything else in the table ran locally with the real DM library (items 16 and 17).

### 22.19 Forward notes (S10b implementation, 2026-09-23)

**Precedence.** These notes record what slice S10b — the "dedicated S10b" §22.15 item 12 asked for —
delivered where the sections above say something else, and what it still leaves. They win over
§0–§21 and over §22.0–§22.17 for the items they name, and for nothing else. (§22.18 is left to slice
S13, written concurrently; this section does not depend on it.)

S10b does not close §22.15's list and was not meant to: that list is five scenarios, fifty mutants
and most suite sub-cases, and one slice that tried all of it would produce exactly the shallow
coverage S10's review found and fixed. It took the part §22.15 item 8 marked as needing **a scenario
and no new engine seam**, and built each piece to the bar S10's review set: a crash enumeration with
§15.3's liveness oracles or a declared replacement, and a mutant registered only after a run injected
it and watched the check fail. Built: **SCN-I** (restore), **SCN-K** (revocation), **SCN-H in part**
(sixteen weeks of generation retention — a publication at every step, not every week — and a late
first flight), and **SCN-G's week-boundary retry** as a
scenario line of its own (`SCN-G-week`); mutants **MC-18, MC-26, MC-28 and MC-33**. The gate line
is `dm mutants: 11 run, 11 detected` and `dm-report-check.sh` pins it. Items 1–6 are what was built;
items 7–10 are what the enumeration and the kill tests found; items 11–13 are the deferrals and what
was verified, by name; item 14 is the adversarial review of the slice and what it changed — items
1–13 are written as they stand after it.

### 22.20 Forward notes (PQ1 and PQ5, 2026-09-23)

**Precedence.** These notes record what the PQ1/PQ5 slice delivered: the two tests of §15.5's PQ row
that §22.15 item 10 deferred from S10 and that §22.18 item 14 found still missing after S11 and S13
(S10b, §22.19, did not build them either). They win over §0–§21 and over §22.0–§22.19 for the items
they name, and for nothing else. Items 1–8 are written as they stand after the slice's adversarial
review; item 9 is that review and what it changed, item 10 what was run after it.

**The one thing to read first.** PM-32 — "the intro inner layer sealed without the X-Wing KEM" — is
now killed by tests of the code, not only by the model (`m1_m3_pqb_mutant_no_kem`, §22.18 item 12).
§22.16 item 18's finding stands: T35's tags cannot see the X-Wing-keyed layer, because `k_in` is never
a `SealKey`, and T35's six Rust tests pass under every one of the six PM-32 patches below (item 5).
What holds PM-32 is the Rust tests. The JVM holds less: PQ1 there is an assertion around every
`openIntro` of the host library, which sees what an **honest** sender's envelopes can show — a key
that ignores the secret or part of it, a wrong number of decapsulations — and nothing that only an
envelope sealed without the KEM would show, because no JVM world carries one (item 7). The table is
the measured state; its third column is what `scripts/gates/pq-mutants.sh` requires of each patch.

| Patch (`client-core/dm/mutants/`) | What it does | Rust tests the gate requires it to fail | PQ1's assertion on the JVM | Run on the JVM |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pm32-k-in-without-kem-secret` | both sides key `k_in` from the transcript alone | 7: PQ1's differential, count and host assertion, the JNI body, PQ5's oracle, sender and gate | refuses it: the perturbed open still opens | at the slice (item 5) and after the review (item 10) |
| `pm32-open-without-decapsulation` | both sides key `k_in` from `SHA-256(ct)`; no decapsulation | 7 | refuses it: no decapsulation | no |
| `pm32-kem-secret-constant` | the X-Wing secret stops depending on the ciphertext, both sides | 7, through PQ5's oracle and the gate envelopes, which then open | **does not see it**: the perturbation lands after the constant | no |
| `pm32-lenient-recipient` | the recipient retries with the all-zero key | 4: PQ1's inner-key count and PQ5's gate | would refuse the retry, but only on an envelope sealed without the KEM | no |
| `pm32-lenient-recipient-own-key` | the recipient retries with a key no gate variant uses | 3: the inner-key count only | as above | no |
| `pm32-zero-secret-on-decapsulation-error` | a failed decapsulation is taken for a zero secret | 4: through the low-order gate variant | as above: it needs a ciphertext that does not decapsulate | no |

|---|---|---|
| 1 | §15.5 PQ1 | **The spy.** `pq::spy` (compiled for the crate's own tests and under the new `ghost-client-dm` feature `pq-spy`, nowhere else) counts per thread every X-Wing decapsulation — both public entry points, `decapsulate` and `decapsulate_with_public`, go through one private `decapsulate_expanded`, counted on entry whatever it returns — every successful encapsulation and every intro inner key derived (`seal::intro_inner_key`, sealing and opening), and can **perturb** the next shared secret either KEM operation returns: one bit flipped, one-shot, either a bit the caller names or the next of the thread's **walk** — byte `n mod 32`, bit `(n / 32) mod 8` for its `n`-th perturbation, a counter, so no randomness is drawn. The perturbation is what makes "`k_in` depends on `ss`" a differential test of the code rather than a property of HKDF: ciphertext, transcript and every other input stay as they were, only the secret the KEM handed back changes. ### 22.21 Forward notes (S11b: the privacy world deepened, 2026-09-23)

**Precedence.** These notes record what slice S11b — a second pass over S11's privacy world, taken
from §22.16's deferrals (items 10–15) — delivered, what it found, and what it left deferred again.
They win over §0–§21 and over §22.0–§22.20 for the items they name, and for nothing else. Where they
revise one of §22.16's items they say so; §22.16 is otherwise unchanged. (§22.19 is slice S10b's and
§22.20 is PQ1/PQ5's, both of which reached `main` first; these notes are numbered after them.) Item 10 records the slice's
adversarial review and what it changed; items 1–9 are corrected in place where it found them wrong.

**The one thing to read first.** NI-DM2 found an **engine defect it did not fix** (item 2): a
TIMER_SET sent before a session exists is stored with the TTL of the **new** timer, not R-T3's larger
one, and the relay can tell such a first flight from a text by its TTL — **a known P-4 and R-T3 leak,
over which the privacy report and the gate are green.** The fix needs the TIMER_SET's bucket kept
with the pending item, which is a schema change and the owner's decision; until then NI-DM2 carries
the case as a **declared open defect**, declared as the exact difference it makes (that one twin's
TTL is 86 400 where the others store 604 800, every other field equal), re-proved on every run and
pinned word for word by the report check, so the check fails the day the defect is fixed or changes
shape, and no other difference can ride on the declaration. What covers that path is **only** this
one twin: JD5 never sees a queued TIMER_SET in the main world (its line says so), and a FAILED item's
retry — the defect's other half — is run by no world. The slice also found a facade gap outside
privacy (item 3) and a gap in S11's model relay (item 4).

S11b is deliberately a **subset** of §22.16's deferrals: one twin (NI-DM2), one hostile mode with the
JD7 variant it exists for, two mutants that became detectable without the redeem lane, HIGH mode or
key changes (PM-5 in its day-rounding half only, PM-31), and NI-DM2 as PM-4's second killer.
Everything else §22.16 items 10–15 defer stays deferred for the reasons given there; item 8 restates
the lists. **Nothing in the report claims a check the run did not make:** `dm-report-check.sh` now
pins NI-DM2 (14 of its 15 twins gating, and the one declared defect exactly), the withhold variant
with a session where a fourth attempt would fall, JD5's split by TIMER_SET path, PM-5's half and
`dm privacy mutants: 12 run, 12 detected`, and refuses S11's ten.

| 1 | §15.6 "Twins" NI-DM2, §21.11 point 3, P-4 | **NI-DM2, built** (`dmworld/NiDm2.kt`). Fifteen twin worlds of the same seed, each a session state crossed with a message kind: **intro** (A scans B at `t0` and M is its first message), **provisional** (B scanned A six hours earlier; at `t0` A's user accepts and M is A's first reply), **pair with its root offer pending** (met in person a day earlier; M is A's first pair message, its own offer riding — §15.6's "first"), **pair after the offer was acknowledged** (A wrote once more and B answered under A's root — §15.6's "later") and **reset** (an established pair; M is the `reset` control, sealed intro mode after the re-establishment); crossed with a **text**, a text **quoting** B's newest message, a **TIMER_SET** (7 d → 1 d, whose R-T3 TTL is 7 d like the text's), a **REACTION** (16 + 1 body bytes) and the **CONTROL**. Pair `k` of clients (A = 2k, B = 2k + 1) carries body length `k` of **0, 17, 2 220, 2 221, 3 000, 14 508, 14 509, 15 000** in every twin that can send it (R-B1's two boundaries, the bodies a text shares with a TIMER_SET, a CONTROL (0) or a REACTION (17), and one length inside each larger class), so a pair's cards, namespaces, relay sets and deposit credentials are the same in every twin. **Compared:** at each length, A's stores into B's inbox from `t0` to `t0 + 20 min` as `(op, relay slot, namespace, size, TTL, credential scope)`, equal as multisets across every **gating** twin with that length (all but the one declared open defect of item 2: 59 of the 60 messages); and — since the review (item 10) — the **second** of each store after `t0`, equal across the twins whose state needs no establishment (provisional and both pair states: 51 messages). **Not compared, declared:** the second of an intro's or a reset's store (it is stored when `EST-READY` runs, which the relay serving the bundle chooses — §21.7 point 6, L7-D6; timing across that choice is NI-DM6's), and the rest of the view (the bundle fetch before an intro is establishment traffic, §1.2); circuits and batch counts, which the model relay does not produce (§22.16 item 2). **What makes it able to fail:** each twin must **reach its variable by the ground truth the ports recorded** — exactly one distinct blob in the compared stores, sealed in the state's mode, of the variant's kind and body length, quoted exactly when the variant quotes, with a root offer riding exactly in the "first" pair state and not in the "later" one (a new `GroundTruth.Content`, recorded at `encodeContent` from the encoder's own `Encoded.Ok` flags and followed through the L1 to the blob). A twin that did not reach its state fails the check and is **not compared** (so an empty view is never a "difference"), and equal views never come from twins that were secretly the same; the first run failed exactly so on the reset twin (item 4). **The PQ-TLV axis is observed, not controlled:** the engine attaches `seal_root_pq` and `pq_key` under the slack rule on its own, and the line prints which TLVs rode on each M (PQ4 in `PqcFlowTest` remains the controlled with/without twin). **Measured** (seed `0x5eed0001`, owner's workstation, 10 s for the fifteen worlds in the full run of item 9, 13 s after the review): 60 messages, 59 of them gating, 51 comparisons of stores and 43 of store seconds (among the 51 messages that need no establishment; every one equal); M sealed INTRO 9, PROVISIONAL 17, PAIR 34; kinds TEXT 28, QUOTED 24, TIMER_SET 4, REACTION 3, CONTROL 1; TLVs that rode none 13, `seal_root` 8, `pq_key` 13, `seal_root` + `pq_key` 13, `seal_root_pq` 5, `seal_root_pq` + `pq_key` 8; sizes by length 4 KiB (0, 17, 2 220), 16 KiB (2 221, 3 000, 14 508), 64 KiB (14 509, 15 000) — every gating twin equal at every length |
| 2 | §10.1 R-T3, R-T4, §7.5, §13.6 `dm_outbound_item`, ME-14 | **An engine defect found and left open: R-T3 on the pending path.** `SendStep`'s send path takes a TIMER_SET's TTL as `DmTimers.timerSetBucket(old, new)`, the larger bucket (R-T3); its **flush of a pending item at `EST-READY`** and its **retry of a FAILED item** take it as `bucketOf(decoded.timerCode)` — the L0 carries only the **new** code, so a TIMER_SET queued before a session exists (a first message, or one sent while re-establishing) is stored at the new bucket. **Reproduced by NI-DM2:** the intro TIMER_SET (7 d → 1 d) is stored with TTL 86 400 at all three relays where every other twin at body length 0 — a quoted empty text, the TIMER_SET in the other three states, the reset control — stores 604 800. **Consequences:** a recipient offline for more than a day never learns of the change (R-T3's purpose), the relay reads the kind of a first flight off its TTL (P-4), and — by the same code, read and not run — a new timer of 1 h makes the flush's deadline check (`deadlineSeconds(author, bucketOf(new))`) fail the item once an establishment takes more than an hour, where R-T4 gives it seven days. It is ME-14's behaviour on those two paths. **Why JD5 never saw it:** the main world sets a timer ten minutes into the establishing session, after `EST-READY`, so no TIMER_SET ever waited for a session. **Why not fixed here:** the old code is gone by the flush (the setter adopted the new timer at the send) and `dm_outbound_item.deadline_hour` cannot recover it (the 7-day cap makes 7 d and 30 d indistinguishable); a fix keeps the TIMER_SET's bucket (or the old code) with the pending item — a column of `dm_outbound_item` and a migration — which is the owner's call. **How the check carries it** (as corrected by the review, item 10): `NiDm2.OPEN_DEFECTS` declares the twin **and the exact difference** — at body length 0, every store of INTRO/TIMER_SET must equal the view every gating twin agrees on with the TTL 604 800 replaced by 86 400, every other field (size, relay slot, namespace, credential scope, number of stores) equal. The twin must reach its variable, and the check **fails** when its stores equal the others' (fixed: remove the entry), carry another TTL (a partial fix or a new bug on the path), differ in any other field, or when the others no longer store 604 800. The report line ends with that one clause, `dm-report-check.sh` pins it word for word at the end of the line, so neither a second declared difference nor another shape of this one passes. **What this leaves uncovered, declared:** the defect itself — **the privacy gate is green over a known P-4 and R-T3 leak** until the engine is fixed; the 1-hour deadline consequence (read, not run); and the FAILED retry path (`SendStep.kt` around line 406), which no world or twin runs. JD5 does not see the pending path: the main world sets its timers ten minutes into the establishing session, after `EST-READY`, and JD5's line now prints how many TIMER_SETs were set over a session and how many were queued (0 in every run measured). Making the defect **fail** the gate instead, or adding a main-world behaviour that sets a timer before the first send (so JD5 fails honestly), were both considered and left to the owner: either turns the PR `android` job red until the schema change lands, and the second also redraws every main-world denominator. **Recommended** (a separate task): the column, the two paths reading it, a `DmFlowTest` case of a first-message TIMER_SET and of a retried FAILED one, and then the main-world behaviour above with the `OPEN_DEFECTS` entry removed |
| 3 | §13.2 facade, §13.6 `dm_message.body_env`, §21.4 rule 5 | **A facade gap outside privacy, found and left open.** `Messaging.send(contact, "", null)` **throws** a `SQLiteException` out of the facade: the codec accepts an empty TEXT (`check_body` bounds only its length and UTF-8), nothing refuses it before `MessageStore.insertMessage`, and `body_env`'s CHECK (`length BETWEEN 30 AND 61485`) refuses the 29-byte envelope of a one-byte flags field. §21.4 rule 5 calls a CHECK abort inside a DM transaction a bug. A **quoted** empty text is stored (the 16-byte reference makes its envelope 45 bytes), so NI-DM2 compares at length 0 a quoted text, a TIMER_SET and a CONTROL, and sends no unquoted empty text. The fix is a facade decision (refuse an empty text with a result, or allow it and lower the CHECK) and is not taken here |

### 22.22 Forward notes (the entitlement world of §15.1 variant (b), 2026-09-23)

**Precedence.** These notes record what the entitlement-world slice delivered — the DM harness
variant (b) of §15.1 that §22.15 items 6 and 7, §22.16 item 10 and §22.19 item 12 name as the one
blocker of **SCN-E**, **JD8** and the **OS** suite — and what those three still need on top of it;
item 12 is the adversarial review of the slice and what it changed, and items 1–11 state the slice
as it stands after it. They win over §0–§21 and over §22.0–§22.21 for the items they name, and for
nothing else. This section depends on none of the slices written concurrently with it (PQ1/PQ5,
§22.20; the S11 continuation, §22.21; S10c, still landing) and was renumbered from its own author's
§22.23 to the number actually free at merge, §22.22.

**The slice is infrastructure and a proof, deliberately not the three consumers.** It builds the
world and shows it works end to end; SCN-E, JD8 and the OS cases are **not** written here (item 8),
and nothing in `DmScenarios.kt`, `Joins.kt`, the report or the gates changes.

### 22.23 Forward notes (S10c implementation, 2026-09-23)

**Precedence.** These notes record what slice S10c — **SCN-C**, one of the two §15.3 scenarios
§22.19 item 12 still named — delivered, what it found and what it leaves. They win over §0–§21 and
over §22.0–§22.22 for the items they name, and for nothing else. (§22.20 is PQ1/PQ5's, §22.21 the S11
continuation's and §22.22 the entitlement world's — all written concurrently with this slice and
landed on `main` first; this section depends on none of them, and was renumbered from its own author's
§22.22 to the number actually free at merge, §22.23.)

S10c builds one scenario whole rather than several in part: SCN-C, with the hostile relay mode its
row names and the bounded fetch-attempt budget of §21.7 point 5 under the crash enumeration, to
pair mode on both sides. **It makes no §15.7 mutant reachable and registers none** — §22.19 item 12
said so before the slice began, and the slice confirms it rather than inventing a claim (item 8);
the gate line stays `dm mutants: 11 run, 11 detected`. What it did find is an **engine defect**: a
message sent to a contact whose three attempt windows were spent was stranded by a process death
between the send's commit and its `EST-START`, and stayed stranded for up to seven days (item 5).
It is fixed here, with a regression test that fails without the fix. The slice's adversarial review
found a second one beside it — a send to a contact that was **still** fetching spent that
contact's attempt budget, so three messages written a minute apart all failed with the first
window — and tightened what SCN-C checks; item 11 records both.

| 1 | §15.1 hostile modes, §21.7 point 6 | **WITHHOLD_NEWEST_BUNDLE** (`ModelDmRelay`). In a bundle namespace the relay never lists the newest bundle it holds and lists every older one as usual. "Newest" is the relay's own notion, the only one it has: the bundle whose **first** deposit is the latest — it cannot open a bundle, but it sees when each one arrived, and a weekly publication is exactly the latest deposit in `P_0`. A copy of the same bytes re-stored later (a publication whose response a timeout lost, re-deposited by the Phase 7 retry) is the same bundle and is withheld with it; keyed on the deposit instead, every timeout run at bob's publication would have served the newest bundle under its first deposit. A namespace is a bundle namespace when its listener registered it for `PREKEYS`, which is what a real relay reads from the shared FETCH read scope every fetcher of a card lists `P_c` under (§5.5, §22.8.7). `withheldNewest` counts the (bundle, listener) pairs it kept back, so a scenario asserts the mode did something; `owed()` does not count them, or every world running the mode would look unsettled for as long as anyone listened. Beside it, `bundleListings`: every list event of a bundle namespace, by node and time — the relay's view of §21.7 point 6's "a listening `P_c` co-occurs with at most three session starts per establishment", which item 3 checks. **Declared narrowing:** the one model relay stands for the whole set of `P_c`, so what is modelled is §21.7 point 6's "a relay set that withholds bundles" — every relay of the set colluding; a set with one honest relay would list the newest bundle, and which of the set's relays withholds is not expressible here (§22.15 item 4) |

An establishment with no later send behaves as before, so no line of the report moved ((g)). What the change can move is on `main`: in JD7's WITHHOLD_ALL_BUNDLES worlds an establishment followed by a second send now has its three windows after that send, which JD7's oracle already allows and which can only add establishments that reach their third window — but this branch does not have those worlds, so it is **not run here** and has to be run on the merge ((h)). A reopening there fetches the older bundle and builds on `g1` before `c1` exists, and every check held. **Fixed:** `stillGivenUp`, just before each attempt to write `c1` (raw reads, no event): still `unreachable`, not listened, not one list event of alice's since the probe — and an every-run check that it ran. Control: a world in which the control itself opens an establishment for alice after bob's publication step fails "… before she wrote c1". (c) **MEDIUM, harness — "`c0` fails with the third window" was checked only at the end of part one.** An `EST-END` that failed the pending items at every close, or a `fail_after_hour` of one hour instead of seven days (a statement rewrite of the `dm_pending_send` insert, which R-T5 then fails at the pass that opens window 2), left `c0` FAILED at the end either way and passed SCN-C and `DmResidueTest`; SCN-C is the only scenario that runs an `EST-END` at all. **Fixed:** `stillWaiting` after every window of part one that closes and every one that opens while alice is fetching, and `DmResidueTest.spendTheBudget` asserts the same between windows. Measured, each as a hand mutation of the production code: the first fails all three spent-budget tests of `DmResidueTest` with "the items still wait after window 1 closed empty", the second with "… when window 2 opens"; the second is also an SCN-C control ("no longer waits while alice is still fetching"). (d) **LOW-MEDIUM — after the `flushStranded` fix nothing could see the user-retry flag of the user-facing paths.** `flushStranded` reopens a stranded item's contact at the next pass, SCN-C's rounds run a pass before the pump, and the regression test calls `SendStep.send` directly; so flipping `userRetry` at `MessagingEngine.retry`, `dispatch` or `resetSession`, or at `ScheduledSteps.runDue`, failed nothing. **Added:** `DmResidueTest.everyActionThatQueuesAnItemReopensAnUnreachableContactAtOnce` checks each of the four right after its call — the scheduled control after the pass that sends it, which runs `flushStranded` **before** the scheduled step, so the recovery cannot be what reopened it. Measured: each of the five call sites flipped to `false`, one at a time, fails a `DmResidueTest` test that names it ("the retry of a FAILED message / a send / a session reset / a due reconnect notice reopens the contact"; the send's also fails (a)'s test; `flushStranded`'s fails "the stranded send's establishment is resumed"). (e) **LOW, harness — the relay-side window checks.** The spacing was measured window start to window start, so a second window five and three quarter hours after the first one closed passed; it is now measured from the last listing of the window before. The oracle is a pure function (`DmScenarios.windowViolations`), and `DmHarnessSelfTest` runs it over listing times written by hand, where the fault-free shape passes and each of its three clauses fails alone — the count clause included, which no engine control reaches, since an engine that lists a fourth window fails an engine-side check first. Two SCN-C controls break a window's shape while everything the engine reports holds — windows one hour apart, windows of thirty minutes — and fail the spacing and the span clause, no earlier check. **Declared, not changed:** the relay's view is sampled only where the script pumps (item 3). (f) **Honesty.** "The first test of it anywhere" (item 3, the regression test's KDoc, the slice's commit message) held against the branch's base only: S11b's JD7 WITHHOLD_ALL_BUNDLES variant on `main` needs establishments that reach their third window and kills PM-31 — item 8 even named it; item 3 now says what S10c adds. "Two new self-test controls show the new checks can fail" overstated them: the unbounded-budget control stops at the engine-side check (item 4; (e) adds the controls that do). The runner extrapolation of `messaging-exit-gate.yml` leaned on S10b's 72 min 51 s having been measured on an idle machine, which nothing recorded, and on the SCN-C-alone figure, which came from a run of an earlier version of the slice (item 10); neither is used now. The per-node message of the pair-acknowledgement check said the opposite of what it checks — `acknowledged` on a node's own offer means that node opened a pair envelope the other side sealed under its root — and is corrected. "The shift is S13's" was measured for SCN-A only, and "every negative was regenerated" was all but `s10-only-gate.txt` (item 10, `self-test.sh`). The slice's commit message said a pending item on an unreachable contact was "necessarily queued by a later user action"; one of the four actions is a scheduled control, which the engine schedules — the code comment and item 5 said so, and the bound holds either way. ### 22.24 Forward notes (T2 at the gate scale after §4.9, 2026-09-23)

**Precedence.** These notes record the half of §4.9 point 3 that §22.16 item 16 left undone — the
gate-scale T2 values after the DM owner namespaces, which §4.9 calls baselines but which **no check
compares a later run with** (item 9(h)) — and what measuring it found. They win over §0–§21 and over
§22.0–§22.23 for the items they name, and for nothing else; where they correct §22.16 item 16 they
say so there. (§22.22 is the entitlement world's and §22.23 is S10c's, both of which reached `main`
first; this section depends on neither.) Nothing here changes the T2 world, a check or a tolerance:
the only files touched are this document, `pass-gate.txt`, `base-gate.txt` (the made-up report the
negative fixtures were made from, kept under its own name), the T2 report cases of `self-test.sh`
and the fixture row of `test-harness/README.md` (items 8 and 10). The section as first written was
reviewed; item 10 says what the review found and what changed.

**The one thing to read first.** Seed pair 0 at the gate scale passes every check after §4.9, with
the same report on the owner's workstation under Windows and in all eight CI runs of it since — the
CI runners being four WSL2 runners on that same laptop (item 1) — and the 26 privacy mutants are
still all detected after the WRITE MISSING correction, in all nine runs since (item 4). **The
gate's ten-seed sweep is not green, and has not been since the first nightly of 2026-09-14:** NI-1d fails on seed
pairs 1 to 5 every night and on pair 9 every night since the second, deterministically — a Phase 8
failure that predates §4.9 and that no section records; the one pair diagnosed, pair 1, traces to
the world's lost-answer fault being drawn from the client's redemption count, which the twin
changes (item 5). And **since §4.9, seed pair 9 also fails NI-1 across cells**, which it passed on
every nightly before (item 6). That one is §4.9's, and it is not a harness bug — recorded, after
the review, from the two worlds' truth: the DM inbox that §4.9 point 2 lists in every relay session
turns the foreground minute sync that Phase 8's payment screen suppresses from an invisible absence
into a gap the relays see, and here the payment (an extra pack bought on ENTITLEMENT_NEEDED)
happened only in the world where an earlier flow had already finalized — an issuer-side event
before the activation cell. It is a design question between two defences, and it is not fixed
here. S4 moved too: it rose on every one of the ten pairs, by 0.016 to 0.025 (ten rises in ten, a
one-sided sign test p ≈ 0.001), far inside its bound but an effect §4.9 point 4's "not a new signal"
did not predict — and both of S1's attackers gained accuracy on every pair with it (item 2). Last,
**the gate job's 240-minute timeout was already being hit before §4.9** (pair 0 cancelled at it four
times from 2026-09-20 on), and §4.9's own cost in runner time is **not measurable** in these runs:
the runner time of one and the same world varies by more than 2× (item 7).

The world models the rule as the design states it (§4.9 point 2's inbox in every session, F8's payment-screen hold), so this is a **design question between two defences**, not a world bug: keeping the inbox heartbeat through the payment screen gives back the co-presence S3d exists to prevent; stopping it shows the gap. ### 22.25 Forward notes (SCN-E: the offline recipient on the entitlement world, 2026-09-24)

**Precedence.** These notes record what the SCN-E slice — the last of §15.3's twelve scenarios no slice
had built, built on the entitlement world of §22.22 — delivered, what it found and what it leaves. They win over
§0–§21 and over §22.0–§22.24 for the items they name, and for nothing else. The slice was written
beside a JD8/privacy-mutant wave that also builds on the entitlement world; this section depends on
nothing that wave writes. It landed as §22.25 — the number its author chose to leave §22.24 free —
and §22.24 was in the event taken by the T2 gate-scale measurement, so the JD8 wave, which lands
after this section, is numbered past it.

SCN-E is built whole — the offline recipient across the week boundaries, `wait_capability`, the
return with its renewal and registrations, the deadline half, and the LOSE_KEYS variant — on the
real redeem and registration lanes, with the oracles every scenario carries. It makes **two** §15.7
mutants reachable and registers both after proving each killed fault-free and at six crash points
inside the window where it acts, beside a clean run (**MC-14** and **MC-15**, items 6 and 14(e));
**MC-22** needs an engine seam and is deferred (item 7). The gate line is `dm mutants: 13 run, 13
detected`. Its crash coverage is **sampled, not every event**, and the report says so in its own
words (item 8). It found **design/engine discrepancies**, recorded and not changed (items 4 and
14(a), (j)), and it answers, by measurement, the engine question §22.22 item 12(s) left for it (item
5). No production code changed. **An adversarial review (two lenses: harness soundness, engine
correctness and honesty) found the first version weaker than it read; item 14 records every finding,
what changed and what was measured, and where an earlier row is wrong it says so and points there.**

| # | Section it implements or corrects | What the SCN-E slice does, and why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | §15.3 SCN-E, §21.2 point 9, §10.1 R-T4 | **The scenario (`ScnE`, variant OFFLINE; `android/messaging/src/test/.../entworld/ScnE.kt`).** alice and bob are genesis identities of the entitlement world, each holding ACCESS tokens of weeks `W0 … W0 + 5` (two per slot per week, `EntClient.addTokens` in the unarmed setup — a trial covers two weeks, and SCN-E needs five), with periodic jobs every 15 minutes; ACTIVATE is §21.12 point 2's resume at the first time-triggered pass. Friday of `W0` (2975): alice scans bob's card in person, turns the conversation's timer **off** (so nothing the oracles read is erased and a stored blob waits 30 days at the relay) and writes; bob accepts and answers; alice answers in pair mode. From Saturday 04:00 bob is **offline** (`Client.offlineWindows`: no network, the phone on, his DM passes and entitlement jobs keep running locally) until Monday 12:00 of `W0 + 4` — across **four** week boundaries, one more than §15.3's three, because a message written after the lapse can outlive its 7-day deadline (R-T4) before bob returns only if he is away for a fourth. bob went offline before his renewal window, so his newest capability is of `W0` and his registrations of `W0` and `W0 + 1` accept deposits until `start(W0 + 3) + 1 h` (§21.2 point 9). alice writes **`e-early`** on Tuesday of `W0 + 1` (registrations live: stored, `SENT`, read by bob three weeks later), **`e-late`** on Wednesday of `W0 + 2`, after `start(W0 + 2) + 1 h`, when only the **`c + 1`** registration of `W0 + 1` still accepts it (stored, `SENT`; added by the review, item 14(d) — the first version deposited nothing there, so the half of the horizon the `c + 1` row buys was never tested), **`e-doomed`** an hour after the lapse (refused at every relay; its deadline passes ten hours before bob returns) and **`e-waiting`** four days after the lapse (it waits; bob returns, redeems week-`W0 + 4` tokens, registers, and it is delivered before its deadline); bob answers once he shows `e-waiting`. **Checked in every run**, from the relay-side record or the clients' rows on the raw connection (so a check is never an event of the run it checks): bob reached no relay while away (the first version's "every accepted deposit of `e-early` made while bob was away" could not fail — `e-early` is written three and a half days after he left — and is gone, item 14(f)); `e-early` and `e-late` each `SENT` with deposits accepted at two relays at least; no deposit of `e-doomed` or `e-waiting` accepted by any relay before bob returned, and alice tried (refused deposits exist); | 4 | §21.2 point 7, CR-16, `ContactKeeper` | **Found by the first run: §21.2 point 7's "refused store attempts are bounded by one retry per session" does not hold on the real engine.** SCN-E's first version checked exactly that sentence — at most one refused store of one client into one namespace at one relay per relay session — and the **unmutated** engine failed it: two refused deposits of alice's at S0 in one foreground session, 64 s apart, under credential generations 62 and 63. The mechanism, read from the code and the run's counters: `ContactKeeper` re-puts a refused credential **at most once per pass**, and it runs on every **time-triggered** pass — the relay session start, the consumer tail after a session, the tail after a quiet run, the in-process timer, a database open — not once per relay session start as §21.2 point 7 says. OFFLINE at S0, generation 17, about 16.7 days in); the control `REFUSAL_IGNORED` (statement rewrites of alice's `CapabilityStore.refuse` for a write credential and of the park) fails the same way; the clean engine, fault-free OFFLINE, parked on all 1 893 of alice's refused stores. **(d) HIGH/MEDIUM, harness — the offline horizon's `c + 1` half was not checked.** Only `e-early` was deposited while bob was away and his registrations lived, in week `W0 + 1`, which the registration of `c` alone covers; and the return check read only the week's row, never the `c + 1` one. The review's mutant — `periods += c + 1` removed from `OwnerSteps.periodsFor` — passed SCN-E. **Fixed:** `e-late` on Wednesday of `W0 + 2`, which only the `c + 1` registration accepts; the relays' held DEPOSIT registrations of bob's read while each message is stored (exactly `{W0, W0 + 1}` for `e-early`, `{W0 + 1}` for `e-late`); the `c + 1` row checked after the return (item 1); a sixth phase for the sample. **Measured:** the mutant, by hand, fails SCN-E fault-free ("while e-early is stored bob's inbox DEPOSIT registrations held at S0 are of weeks [2975], expected [2975, 2976] …"), and — the review's unrun guess — `EntDmWorldTest` also fails, five of its seven tests ("the fetch registration of week 2976 of its bundle at S0 is not done, held and paid for …"). **(e) MEDIUM, harness — the kills' crash points fell before the mutants act.** Spread over every event both worlds reach, all six of MC-15's and five of MC-14's were in the establishment; the review ran MC-15 at ten points inside its window and it survived one (crash@44 510: the reboot counted as a trigger and the rule excused the next re-put). **Fixed:** the six points are spread over the window from the loss (the mutated run's own mark) to the fault-free failure, printed with the window; every point killed, beside a clean run that passes (item 6); the kill rule the report prints says so ("… between the loss and its fault-free failure …"), and `dm-report-check.sh` pins it. **(f) LOW — checks that could not fail, or were not shown to.** "Every accepted deposit of `e-early` made while bob was away" could not fail (`e-early` is written three and a half days after he left): removed, and "bob reached no relay while away" checked instead. "bob's registrations were his only ones" was written in a comment and not checked: now the held-registration check of (d). The end-of-run clauses on `e-waiting` are **declared** backstops no control reaches on its own: every world that breaks them fails an earlier check first (item 3). **(g) MEDIUM — "the oracles, all on" was overstated:** CS-2 and CS-4 were missing (and the no-loss oracle compared sets). **Added:** CS-2 at the end of every run (`DmCrashRunner.displayedAtMostOnce`'s position check, and no inbound text rendered twice) and CS-4 across runs (the render order of every faulted run of the sample against the recording run's). T28 has no check in SCN-E, declared (item 11(i)). **(h) MEDIUM — the sample never landed inside a store lease.** The review made Phase 7's lease recovery (M1, `OutboxStore.normalizeLeases`) a no-op: it passed all 24 gate-scale sampled points of LOSE_KEYS with alice armed, and crashing at each of alice's 16 stores caught 6. **Fixed:** each picked store is also crashed at its after-apply event (a death with the lease in flight), and a new end check — no store lease in flight once the tail has quiesced — sees a lease left on a message already `SENT` through its other relays. **One claim of the review's was false:** that the events before the first phase mark (the initial boot and migration) were never sampled. The first mark is event 0 in every recording — the first boot runs while the scenario builds, before the runner arms the bus, so its events are not events of the run — and the first stratum started there; the strata now start at event 0 by construction all the same. **Measured** (by hand, the M1 no-op applied, a crash at each point): before the new end check, LOSE_KEYS alice failed at 6 of all 16 store points (the review's figure), and of the gate's picks LOSE_KEYS bob at 1 of 3, OFFLINE alice at 6 of 15 and OFFLINE bob at 3 of 9; with it, at **46 of 46** (all 16 of alice's and all 6 of bob's LOSE_KEYS stores, the gate's 15 and 9 picks of OFFLINE); the clean engine at the same 46 points, at 0. **(i) LOW — report labelling and the report check.** The header printed "scale: gate (every event)" and "slices S10, S10b and S10c" over the sampled lines: it now names SCN-E and carries a coverage line ("the scale is the density of the dm crash classes lines; the dm crash sample lines (SCN-E) are sampled, not every event"), which the check requires. The check held the SCN-E lines to "at least" rules — "8 singles over 1 phases, 1 timeouts over 12 stores" was accepted as a gate line: it now pins each line's phases (six, three), its density per phase, and its store faults per phase (item 8). `self-test.sh`'s comment called both positives real reports; `pass-gate.txt` is assembled (item 13), and the comment says so. Item 5's "one per relay per session" is "about one, at most two" (598 per relay over 591 sessions). Item 4's "which is the part CR-16 is about" and this slice's summary's "the relay's refusal never drives the retry" claimed more than the first rule checked; (b) and (c) are what now check it. **(k) Verified after the review, on the code as committed.** Local runs on the owner's Windows workstation (24 logical CPUs, the harness at 8 worker threads); `ghost_dm_host.dll` from `cargo build -p ghost-dm-host --release --locked` of this tree, which had nothing to rebuild (the review changes no Rust and no production code). **PR scale, the whole `:messaging` suite** (item 13's command), 22 min 6 s: **251 tests in 28 classes, 0 failures, 0 errors, 20 skipped** — exactly the privacy worlds `-Dghost.dm.privacy=off` switches off (`DmPrivacyMutantTest` 13, `DmPrivacyWorldTest` 7) — and the **53 harness and entitlement-world tests with 0 skipped** (`ScnETest` 5, `EntDmWorldTest` 7, `DmCrashEnumerationTest` 13, `DmHarnessSelfTest` 10, `DmMutantDetectionTest` 11, `DmPoisonTest` 3, `DmSeededWorldTest` 2, `DmSuiteTest` 2); `:sync` and `:entitlement` (sources untouched; their test sources compile into `:messaging`'s run) |

### 22.26 Forward notes (JD8 and the privacy mutants of the redeem lane, 2026-09-24)

**Precedence.** These notes record what the JD8 slice delivered — **JD8** (§15.6) as a twin
comparison on the entitlement world of §22.22, its report lines, check and gate wiring, and the
three privacy mutants of §15.7 a JVM world reaches only through the redeem lane (**PM-1**,
**PM-1b**, and **PM-26**'s later-weeks half) — what it measured, what the adversarial review of it
changed (item 13), and what it leaves deferred or open (items 8, 10 and 14). They win over §0–§21
and over §22.0–§22.25 for the items they name, and for nothing else. §22.22 item 8 named JD8's
remaining work, and §22.16 items 10 and 15 and §22.21 item 8 deferred JD8 and seven redeem-lane
mutants; this section revises those items where it says so. The slice was written beside the T2
gate-scale wave and the SCN-E wave as "§22.24"; §22.24 went to the T2 notes and §22.25 says the JD8
wave is numbered past it, so on the merge of `main` into this branch every reference the slice made
— the report line, the check's pinned declaration, the fixtures, the Kotlin notes, both workflows,
`self-test.sh` — became §22.26, and the report and every fixture are a run of the merged code (item
12). It touches the files it shares with those waves only additively (item 9).

**The one thing to read first: JD8 compares each call's time at the finest grain this harness can
test — a registration to the minute, a redemption to the relay session it ran in — and a
redemption's minute is declared untestable here, not shown to leak.** The first version of this
slice measured T27's minute, reported it, gated on none of it, and wrote that the minute "does not
hold" between twins and that "either the row or the engine has to change". The review showed both
were wrong in kind (item 13(a), (b)). A JD8 that gates no time passes a leak that moves a renewal by
ten hours, or a later week's registrations by two days, according to the traffic a client received:
the review built two such leaks, each keeping every count equal, and both passed the first version;
they are now registered controls that JD8 fails by its timing clause alone (item 4). And what was
measured does not show an engine leak. On three seeds (item 3) **no registration pair moved minute
and every redemption pair ran in the same relay session**; five redemption pairs moved inside their
session — on the third seed by 17 s, 52 s, 3 s and 9 ms, two of them across a minute, and on the
second by 3 s. The harness hands each call site its n-th random draw in call order (`SiteRandom`),
so DM work that holds a session open for more redeem-lane steps shifts that lane's later draws in the
twin that has it: a property of how the twins share their randomness, which says nothing either way
about a device, whose draws are fresh. This harness cannot test a redemption's minute. **Open, for
the owner** (items 3 and 14): whether T27's "minute" is meant for redemptions or should read
"session", as JD8 now checks it; and one engine path, found by the review and exercised by no world,
by which the length of a background relay session could depend on DM state.

| # | Section it implements or corrects | What the JD8 slice does, and why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | §15.6 JD8, §14.1 T27, §13.4 (NI-K row) | **The twins** (`entworld/EntDmJd8.kt`, `Jd8Twin`). The entitlement world of §22.22 with **five clients**, each with the real entitlement engine (trial through the real issuer lane, the redeem lane against one `ModelRedeemRelay` per ES slot) and the real DM stack over the same database, on the four slot relays: alice (armed), bob, carol and erin activate a trial at 1, 3, 5 and 7 minutes; **dave holds no token** (`genesis`: his identity exists, his DM layer activates by §21.12's resume and has a card alice scans in person, and he registers nothing — a contact who never bought access; the only calls relays saw from him are 6 `LIST`s in each twin, the same in both, on each of the three seeds, and no `REDEEM`, `REGISTER` or `STORE`; the first version's class note said he "publishes a card", item 13(k)). Periodic jobs every 15 minutes for all five; the trial is 8 tokens per slot and week (`trialPerSlot = 8`; the world's default is 2), so a mutant that spends tokens on contacts does not starve the owner's own renewals and change the world for that reason instead. The world runs from the Friday of access week 2975 at 08:00 to `start(2976) + 3 h` (67 h), so every trace holds the first redemptions (week 2975), the Friday capability's `c` and `c + 1` registrations, the renewal with week-2976 tokens at the planner's EXPIRING PRF time on Sunday, and the renewal's `c + 1` rows (week 2977); the second renewal (week-2977 tokens) falls after the horizon and is in neither trace. **The twins differ in the DM activity and nothing else:** the same seed, trials, jobs and **foreground sessions** in both (the user opens the app at the same minutes whether or not it writes); in the **active** twin alice scans the four cards in person at 6 h and writes to each, the three reachable contacts accept and answer, alice writes again, sends bursts on Saturday, and all Sunday — the renewal window — one of the three writes to her every hour and she answers half an hour later (three texts each way every fourth hour), and after the boundary all four write once more: **95 texts, 94 of them to or from a reachable contact, all delivered**. dave's establishment runs its three windows out (his bundle namespace has no FETCH registration, so the relays refuse alice's credential): alice holds a **LOCAL need** for the rest of the run, the need §13.4's planner must never redeem, which is what makes PM-1b reachable (item 6) — a **read** need, so no LOCAL **write** need exists in either twin (item 14). In the **idle** twin nobody adds anybody and nobody writes. The active twin's DM actions are adds by QR, accepts, texts written and received, and one unreachable contact; no rejection, deletion, key change, reset, restore or invite (item 10(h)). **Compared**, for alice, bob, carol and erin — each differs between the twins in its own DM activity: alice 0 vs 4 contacts, each of the others 0 vs 1 — the multiset of every `REDEEM` and `REGISTER` a relay saw, as (kind, relay, namespace, token week or registration period, key kind): T27's count, relay and namespace and §15.6's week, which must be equal; in each twin, every one of those calls on a namespace the client owns (§15.6's "only own namespaces", JD3's redeem-and-register clause); and each call's time (item 3). dave's trace must be empty in both. **Narrower than §13.4's "0 and 30 contacts"**: 4 contacts (item 10) |
| 2 | §15.6 JD8 (the view it reads), §22.22 item 3 | **The trace is the world's relay record, plus what it does not carry: a `RegisterKey`'s arguments and each call's relay session.** `REDEEM` and `REGISTER` calls come from `EntDmWorld.relayEvents` (after-apply and reached: what relays received, recorded through `World.relayObserver` before any fault plan or hook), a `REDEEM`'s week from the issued token (`EntRecords.issued`). A `RegisterKey` also names a period and a key kind, which "the week" needs: they are **the arguments the harness's relay port handed the model relay** — `HarnessRelayPort.registerKey` puts `(periodId, kind.code)` into the call's `CallInfo.registration` before it calls `ModelRelay.registerKey` with the same two values — and an after-apply `REGISTER` event without them is counted and fails JD8 (0 in every run). The first version read them from the client's own `relay_key_registration` row whose lease was in flight and called that "exactly the arguments the call carried", which was inferred, not checked (item 13(g)); this is the slice's one change to the `:sync` harness (`Core.kt`'s `CallInfo` gains a nullable field that defaults to null, and no other call, digest or check reads it). Each call also gets the **start time of the relay session it was made in** (`World.onSessionStart`, chained after `EntDmWorld`'s hooks): the jobs and the foreground schedule are the same in both twins, so the same session starts at the same millisecond in both, and a session is identified across the twins by that time |
| 3 | §14.1 T27 ("minute"), §22.22 item 8 | **The time of each call: measured, and compared at the grain the harness can test.** Each call of a key is paired with the same key's call of the other twin in time order. **Compared:** every registration pair must fall in the **same minute**; every redemption pair must run in the **same relay session** (identified by its start time, item 2; a call outside any session matches nothing). **Reported, not compared:** the redemption pairs in the same minute, all pairs at the same millisecond, and how many of the active twin's calls came after a message — any call on a contact's namespace, or a `GET` of the own inbox — in their own relay session. **Measured on the seeds `0x5eed0001`, `0x5eed0002` and `0x5eed0003`** (the committed code, the report's configuration): registrations 138 of 138, 134 of 134 and 138 of 138 pairs in the same minute; redemptions **48 of 48 in the same session on each seed**, and 48, 48 and **46** of 48 in the same minute; 186 of 186, 181 of 182 and 182 of 186 pairs at the same millisecond; 6, 8 and 6 pairs after a message in their session, all redemptions. The pairs that moved, all redemptions and all inside the session the idle twin redeemed them in: on the second seed alice's week-2976 renewal at S3 of her inbox 3 s earlier in the active twin; on the third, alice's renewals at S0 of her inbox and of her bundle namespace 16.8 s and 51.5 s earlier (each across a minute, each after she had fetched or stored messages in that session), one of alice's 9 ms earlier, and **bob's 3 s earlier in a session in which nothing had moved a message**. **Why the minute of a redemption cannot be tested here.** The first version measured, on the third seed, that alice's lane had drawn `RedeemLane#nextWait` 927 times in the active twin and 925 in the idle one (963 and 963 on the first seed; not re-measured here), and `SiteRandom` hands each call site its n-th draw in call order: DM work that holds a session open for more lane steps shifts every later wait of that lane in that twin, and the step at which a due renewal comes up with it. bob's move, with no message before it in its session, fits a shifted draw sequence and not a message. So the twins are coupled through their randomness in a way that moves a redemption's minute by itself, and a device, whose draws are fresh, has no such coupling: the measurement says nothing either way about whether the engine's redemption minute depends on DM activity, and the first version's "T27's minute does not hold … either the row or the engine has to change" went further than the data (item 13(b)). No registration moved on any seed: in STANDARD mode the work lane registers in a session's first maintenance pass, before that pass's stores (`WorkItem.Pass`, "registrations first"), and the DM layer creates the renewal's `c + 1` rows at a time-triggered pass, so each registration ran before anything of its session moved a message. **Open, for the owner:** whether T27's row should say "session" for redemptions, as JD8 now checks, or keep "minute" and gain a harness whose twins do not share draws by call order (or an engine whose redemption time is a PRF of the session rather than a running draw — an engine change, not this slice's); and item 14. JD8 pins the declaration word for word (item 9), so a line that claimed the redemption minute compared fails the check |
| 4 | §15.6 JD8, §15.6 "Report" | **What keeps JD8 from passing vacuously, comparing a world with itself, or passing a timing leak.** JD8 fails without comparing when the twins did not reach their variable: the active twin's alice must hold her four contacts; every text of the three reachable contacts must be `SENT` at its sender and shown by its recipient; each of the four token holders must have made relay calls on its contacts' namespaces (550 in all on the first seed); dave's establishment must not be `READY` (it is `UNREACHABLE`); both twins must run to their horizon with the world's end checks (structural invariants of every client, `EntWorld.structural`, no DM pass threw); the idle twin's clients must hold no contact and make **no** call on a DM namespace they do not own; and every `RegisterKey` must have its arguments. The first version held its kills against the checked run and rested the equivalence on one hand measurement (item 13(f)). **The world runs to a fixed horizon, not to the Phase 7 quiescence**: dave's refused credential leaves alice a LOCAL need and a FAILED text for good, which the quiescence oracles rightly refuse |

The contact KEEPER re-puts a `rejected` credential at most once per pass (§21.2 point 7, MC-15) and never an `exhausted` one (§4.5: the recipient's quota, not the sender's credential; `ContactKeeper.install`). So **a contact whose DEPOSIT credential is exhausted is a lasting LOCAL write need**, and one whose deposits the relays keep refusing — a recipient who stopped paying, whose refused deposits §22.22 item 12(s) and SCN-E (§22.25) saw retried — is one at each session start that follows a refusal, since the count is read before that session's DM pass re-puts the credential. While either lasts, **every background session of the sender is held** to its redeem lane's first step: a background session's length, which a relay sees as the time its circuits stay open, then depends on the sender's DM state. What this does **not** establish, read from the code and not run: whether any redemption or registration moves. A session that starts with an own write need pending — every session in which a renewal is due — is armed by that need anyway, so a LOCAL need changes the arming only of sessions that start with no own write need, whose first lane step has no own renewal to redeem unless one comes due within its held seconds. The reviewer's reading, that the step which redeems a due renewal then depends on DM state, is plausible for that corner and is not measured; T27's list (count, minute, relay and namespace of redemptions and registrations) does not name session length, so whether a DM-dependent session length is a leak the design forbids is itself the question. **Not run anywhere:** in JD8's twins alice's only LOCAL need is dave's refused FETCH credential, a **read** need, and no contact's inbox refuses deposits or runs out of quota. §13.4's "LOCAL needs are never redeemed" is kept — the planner still skips them — so this is about the hold, not the planner. T27's "below quota exhaustion" may be meant to cover the exhausted case; it does not cover the refused one. **For the owner:** whether the hold should count only REDEEM-source write needs (a one-line change of `pendingWriteNeeds` that changes when background sessions end for every client, so it needs its own review and the Phase 8 hold's tests), or whether a session held by a LOCAL need is acceptable; and whether a JD8 variant whose active twin writes to a contact who has stopped paying — which would measure the session length and the redemptions beside it — should be built |

### 22.27 Forward notes (functional suite cases under the crash enumeration: KC12, RS2 and RP7; mutants MC-21 and MC-24, 2026-09-24)

**Precedence.** These notes record what the suite-case slice — §15.5's functional sub-cases that
§22.15 items 7 and 8, §22.19 item 12 and §22.25 item 12 left outside the harness — delivered, what
it measured and what it leaves. They win over §0–§21 and over §22.0–§22.25 for the items they name,
and for nothing else. The slice was written beside a JD8/privacy wave (which takes §22.26), a T2
diagnosis wave and a documentation wave; this section depends on nothing any of them writes, and
its additions to `dm-report-check.sh` and `self-test.sh` are blocks of their own.

Built: three §15.5 sub-cases as crash scenarios, each run fault-free and under the enumeration with
the runner's three standing oracles on — **KC12** (a requester sending two identities: no crash,
no state change), **RS2** (a client offline 60 days — 61 here, item 11(a): blobs past TTL lost and
declared, blobs within it delivered, pair envelopes open after the absence) and **RP7** (an old L0
re-sealed under a later week key — built narrower, as a back-dated L0 its sender seals, item 3) —
and the two §15.7 mutants the first two make reachable, **MC-24** (`request → changed` attempted)
and **MC-21** (pair keys erased before ratcheting forward), each registered only after a run killed
it fault-free and at crash points inside the transaction it first changes, beside a clean run at
each point (item 6 as item 11(c) corrected it). The adversarial review of the slice is item 11.
RP7 has **no** registered mutant: §15.7's MC-9 is out of every mechanism's reach (item 8). The gate
line is `dm mutants: 15 run, 15 detected`. No production code changed; no engine defect was found
(item 9).

The literal RP7 — a holder of `K_w` and `K_{w+1}` re-sealing an undelivered week-`w` envelope's L1 under `K_{w+1}` — was not built, and the KDoc quoted `ReceiveStep`'s code comment as §7.6. **Declared, not built:** item 3 and the KDoc now say what is built (the sender-side construction: a fresh, back-dated L0), why it is the same input at bob up to B1's decision, and what the literal case adds after it (the genuine copy failing at Olm once R8 consumed its key); item 8 names the construction that would build it and why it was not; the KDoc quotes §7.6's table. **(g) LOW — two declared losses were unconditional.** KC12 and RP7 declared their lost text up front, against `DmScenario.declaredLoss`'s rule. **Fixed:** KC12 declares the second identity's message once bob's decision has found it written, `SENT`, owed by no relay and consumed while the contact was a request; RP7 declares the back-dated message once the decorator has back-dated its L0 in the run. **(h) LOW — MC-21's KDoc said the no-loss and liveness oracles stand behind its kill;** the runner reads a scenario's own checks before either, so no run reached them. Its crash half now accepts the in-key check's message alone, and the KDoc says why. **(i) LOW — "four controls for the checks no registered mutant reaches" overstated.** Item 10 of `DmHarnessSelfTest` had one control each for four checks. With the review's three (KC12's whole-state check, RS2's gap and its every-week key check) it covers seven; these checks still have **no control that makes them fail**, declared: RS2's fault-free "no bundle listing", "current sessions unchanged" and "no `unknown_seal`"; KC12's "no pending identity", "no held row", "pinned unchanged", "exactly one `request_key_mismatch`" and "nothing poisoned" (the accepted-first control fails at the trust check before them); RP7's "exactly one `stale`", "dated before the key's week" and "inside R9's bound"; and RS2's day-40 render check. **(j) LOW — the report check.** `dm-report-check.sh` accepted any `dm suite cases: N run` with N ≥ 1 (a four-case report passed, measured): it now pins seven. Two new negatives, `suite-old-case-count` and `mc21-first-window-rule` (MC-21 held to the first version's rule). **(k) Verified after the review, on the code as committed.** Local runs on the owner's Windows workstation (24 logical CPUs, the harness at 8 worker threads), with sibling waves' builds and the review's own parallel runs sharing the machine, so every time is that load's; `ghost_dm_host.dll` from `cargo build -p ghost-dm-host --release --locked` of this tree, which had nothing to rebuild (the review changes no Rust and no production code). **Targeted first** (`DmSuiteTest.suiteCasesPassFaultFree`, `DmHarnessSelfTest`, the MC-21 and MC-24 kills): all green, 1 min 49 s. **PR scale, the whole `:messaging` suite** (item 10's command), 46 min 30 s: **255 tests in 28 classes, 0 failures, 0 errors, 20 skipped** — exactly the privacy worlds `-Dghost.dm.privacy=off` switches off (`DmPrivacyMutantTest` 13, `DmPrivacyWorldTest` 7) — and the **57 harness and entitlement-world tests with 0 skipped** (`ScnETest` 5, `EntDmWorldTest` 7, `DmCrashEnumerationTest` 13, `DmHarnessSelfTest` 12, `DmMutantDetectionTest` 13, `DmPoisonTest` 3, `DmSeededWorldTest` 2, `DmSuiteTest` 2). Its report is the new `pass-pr.txt`, **unedited**, and differs from the previous one in exactly three lines — RS2's (11 053 events, 851 singles, 1 timeout over 10 stores), MC-21's and MC-24's (the rule of item 6) — every other line, SCN-E's four and the six other suite cases' included, byte-identical: the fixes of (b) change nothing a clean run does. **Kills** (in the PR run, identical in the targeted run): MC-21 — the clean RS2 passes (11 053 events), the mutated one fails at event 10 897 with the return-week in-key check; the mark is at 4 034 and the first transaction the rewrite changes is bob's SWEEP, events 4 047–4 092; at crash@4 047, 4 056, 4 065, 4 074, 4 083 and 4 092 the mutated run fails with the same message after one crash injected and one reboot, the clean run passing at each; MC-24 — the clean KC12 passes (4 903 events), the mutated one fails at event 539; the mark is at 451 and the transaction is the RECV at events 516–517 (the rewritten read, and the `UPDATE` the schema refuses, where it rolls back); at crash@516 and 517 the same. **Gate scale, the seven suite cases** (`--rerun --tests "org.ghost.messaging.harness.DmSuiteTest" -Dghost.dm.crash=full`, on a copy of the tree, beside the PR run): **2 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped**, 51 min 13 s, the enumeration test 47 min 35 s of it — RS2 11 053 singles of 11 053 events and 10 timeouts over 10 stores, and RP6, RP9, CB-reject-replay, EP-read-expiry, KC12 and RP7 byte-identical to the previous `pass-gate.txt`: 22 750 single-crash runs and 22 timeout-after-apply runs, every one passing every check and oracle, the reboot check of (b) included. **The whole gate was not run** (as in item 10), so **`pass-gate.txt` is assembled**: the previous one with the RS2 line of the run above and the PR run's MC-21 and MC-24 lines (a kill rule does not depend on the scale). **Hand mutants** (a throwaway toggle in a scratch copy of the production code; none committed): the cap back at eight ((a)), the review's two KC12 mutants ((d)) and the ratchet storing only the newest week ((e)), with the results quoted there; and RS2 at 60 days, clean or with the cap at eight, fails the gap check: "bob came back in week 2878, 8 week-indices after his newest in-key (week 2870)". **Negatives:** every negative but `s10-only-gate.txt` regenerated from the new positives by replacing, wherever a negative carries it verbatim, each of the six lines the positives changed (RS2's, MC-21's and MC-24's, at each scale), and by hand in the three whose own change is on one of them (`no-timeouts`, `relay-event-denominator`, `mc21-weakened-kill-rule`); each then checked to differ from its positive by as many lines as before, and the new files to hold no 10 792 and no "60-day"; two new ((j)). **`self-test.sh`'s 78 `dm-report-check` cases** (the 76 before and the two new), extracted and run exactly as its `dmr_case` runs them, sixteen at a time: 78 ok, 0 wrong (24 min 58 s) — each positive accepted and each negative refused, every refusal read for the reason its case names. The rest of `self-test.sh` (its other gates' cases, none of whose scripts or fixtures the review touches) was not run. **Static gates** (`scripts/gates/run-all.sh`, `workflow-yaml` through WSL): all fifteen OK (`apk-no-debug-hooks` without its mapping half, which needs a release build's `mapping.txt`; `workflow-yaml` read the workflow after this review's comment edit). **Not run:** the whole gate; the privacy suite (untouched); `:sync` and `:entitlement` (sources untouched; their test sources compile into `:messaging`'s run). |

### 22.29 Forward notes (S14: the documents of §16.4, 2026-09-24)

**Precedence.** These notes record what the documents part of slice S14 applied from Appendix B
(§16.4's list) and how it was reconciled with what Phase 9 actually built (§22.9–§22.26). They win
over §16.4, §17.2 item 15 and Appendix B for the items they name, and for nothing else. They were
written on branch `p9-docs` from `main` at `f21f534`; the adversarial review of the documents
(item 7) found `main` had moved to `afda7e7` with §22.26 (JD8, PM-1, PM-1b and PM-26's later-weeks
half), so `main` was merged into the branch and every document now states the state **at
`afda7e7`**. §22.27 and §22.28 are left to waves written concurrently; anything they change — the
mutant counts, a report line, a join — has to be re-read when they merge. No production code
changed except the two comments of B.1.

**The one thing to read first.** Appendix B was drafted as the text of a *closed* phase. It is
applied here as the text of a phase that is **in progress with its exit gate not met**: every
invariant row says what verification exists today (built and run, built and not run, not built),
`docs/STATUS.md` reads "în lucru; poarta de ieșire nu e îndeplinită", and no document states a
quantum-resistance property as an assurance (CP-10, §9.8): PQ-A/PQ-B/PQ-C are described as
design and implementation with PQ-R1 … PQ-R8 declared, and every PQ sentence says that the models
have never run and that the external review has not happened. Where the draft contradicted a
forward note, the note won and the divergence is in item 2.
